title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck's continuation of La Longue Marche. He is looking for solutions of a 'loop relation' (157), [α,ρ] = ε[β,σ]ε₁(μ−1), inside a linear algebraic group G. The notation is as follows. ΓX denotes sections or points. ρ and σ are elements of G, or of normalizers of the tori T_ρ and T_σ, acting on G by inner conjugation: ρ(u) = ρuρ⁻¹, and [u,ρ] = u·ρ(u)⁻¹. ε, ε₁ and ε₀ are strict unipotents; ε₁(t) is read as a one-parameter additive subgroup G_a → G. T₀ is a torus, μ = det(u) for u ∈ ΓT₀, and L₀ is a unipotent line, the image of ε₀.

The page analyses the two conditions extracted on the previous page.
(158a) b⁻¹σ(b) = ε_σ(b) for b in the normalizer N_σ, i.e. b acting on σ gives ε_σ(b)·σ.
(158b) [u,ρ] = [u,σ]ε₁(μ−1) for all u ∈ ΓT₀. Equivalently ρ(u) = ε₁(1−μ)σ(u), and after conjugating by σ⁻¹, σ⁻¹ρ(u) = ε₀(1−μ)·u with ε₀ = σ⁻¹(ε₁).

He concludes as follows. Suppose T₀ normalizes L₀ and σ⁻¹ρ ∈ ΓT₀·L₀, which is Borel-like. Then (158b) holds when (159a) σ⁻¹ρ = ε₀·u₀ with u₀ ∈ ΓT₀, and (159b) T₀ acts on L₀ through the character det.

Check: if u ε₀(s) u⁻¹ = ε₀(μs) and T₀ is commutative, then
(ε₀(1)u₀) u (ε₀(1)u₀)⁻¹ = ε₀(1) u ε₀(−1) = ε₀(1)ε₀(−μ)u = ε₀(1−μ)u.
That is exactly the required identity.

He then notes that (159) appeared 'comme des cheveux sur la soupe' (unmotivated). There should be a more conceptual derivation, possibly via the conjugation conditions of section VII.

He therefore restates everything as (160), formulas for the action of U on ρ, σ and ε₀:
- U(ρ) = int(α₀)ρ, i.e. [U,ρ] = αρ(α)⁻¹;
- U(σ) = ε·int(β₀)σ, i.e. [U,σ] = εβσ(β)⁻¹;
- U(ε₀) = ε₀(μ), i.e. U scales L₀ by μ = det U, a consequence of (159b).

On the next page these are verified, and the loop relation (157) is recovered from them by a formal computation. This is a sufficiency criterion: a 'Borel-type' ansatz producing solutions of the loop equation in a linear group.
errors: No substantive error. The deduction from (159a,b) to (158b) is correct once T₀ is commutative and acts on L₀ via det.

The step from (158b) to σ⁻¹ρ(u) = ε₀(1−μ)u requires reading ε₀ = σ⁻¹(ε₁) as the conjugated one-parameter subgroup σ⁻¹ε₁(·)σ, not a single element. The notation slides between ε₀ as an element (ε₀ = ε₀(1) in 159a) and as a homomorphism G_a → G.

Grothendieck himself flags sign issues ('attention aux signes'). The sign conventions in the commutator [u,ρ] versus ε₁(μ−1)/ε₁(1−μ) are consistent on this page, but (160)'s third formula is hard to read and is restated as ε₀(μ) on the next page.
(159) is only a sufficient condition (an ansatz), not a characterization. Grothendieck acknowledges remaining freedom ('il y a quand même encore de la marge').

ideas.what: Reduction of a twisted commutator ('loop') relation to a Borel-type ansatz: σ⁻¹ρ = ε₀u₀ in T₀·L₀, with T₀ acting on the root line L₀ via the character det
ideas.modern_name: Solving commutator equations in a Borel subgroup (torus acting on a root subgroup by a character)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard linear algebraic group theory (Chevalley, Borel)

ideas.what: Linear (matrix-group) models of the 'équation des lacets' satisfied by Galois/Teichmüller actions on fundamental groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Grothendieck's own loop-equation work is unpublished
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses the Teichmüller tower; this linear variant probably not

missed.claim: Grothendieck finds the sufficient condition (159) unmotivated. He calls for a more conceptual derivation of solutions of the loop equation in linear groups, possibly linked to the conjugation conditions of section VII. On the next page he only verifies it formally.
missed.quote: Mais ici l'équation (159) venait un peu comme des cheveux sur la soupe – il doit y avoir des façons plus convaincantes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A conceptual classification of solutions of GT/loop-type relations in reductive groups (e.g. GL₂, SL₂) would bear on linear images of GT-type groups. However, this specific computation is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine group-theoretic verification inside a long unpublished computational manuscript. It is interesting as a document of Grothendieck's linear approach to the loop equation, but contains no result a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Il résulte de l'ensemble des deux conditions'.
'ce qui s'écrit aussi (en multipliant à gauche par σ⁻¹ les deux membres)'.
The ansatz is 'si σ⁻¹ρ ∈ ΓT₀·L₀, est de la forme'.
Read: 'Il y a quand même encore de la marge, par rapport aux conditions des conjugaisons analogues des VII ?'.
Read: 'Mais ici l'équation (159) venait un peu comme des cheveux sur la soupe – il doit y avoir des façons plus convaincantes et exigeantes de ...'.
In (160) the acting element is underlined capital U (Ū), not lowercase u: U(ρ) = int(α₀)ρ (= α₀ρ(α₀)⁻¹ρ), U(σ) = ε·int(β₀)σ.
The third line of (160) likely reads U(ε₀) = int(f⁻¹)(ε₀(...)), not int(ℓ(ρ)⁻¹), since the next line refers to U = f⁻¹u.
Read: 'La troisième relation résulte de l'égalité U = f⁻¹u, et du fait que par hypothèse (159 b) U ∈ ΓT₀ opère sur L₀ (identiquement) via la multiplication par μ = det(U)'.
In (158a), N_σ is presumably the normalizer of T_σ: 'identiquement si b ∈ ΓN_σ'.
